title: Raincheck capacity & staffing fairshare analysis
body:
Executive summary:

Quick snapshot: this is a compact budgeting + HC plan focused on how we absorb short (6–12 week) price shocks and longer (6–12 month) pricing erosion while preserving SLA-backed Dedicated capacity and minimizing layoffs. Aim: produce a compact decision matrix (token price delta -> hiring / burst-reserve action) and a sensitivity table that ties price moves to runway and gross margin.

High-level takeaways (working):
- Small price compression (-10% per-token) can be absorbed via aggressive quantization + prefix/KV cache improvements (targeted savings ~8–12% cost/token) and deferring non-critical hires for 8–12 weeks.
- Medium compression (-25%) forces either pricing action (discounts removal / feature gating) or ~15% HC reduction in non-customer-facing roles if burst reserves not increased.
- Large compression (-40% or sustained) requires a combination of price tier changes, deeper HC cuts, and delaying Dedicated capacity expansion.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Baseline token cost per 1k tokens: $0.42 (mix of hosted/dedicated/on-prem weighted by current revenue mix).
- Revenue per 1k tokens: $1.20 baseline (mix of embedding, gen, chat).
- Current runway (cash) for finance model: 14 months at run-rate without changes.
- Hiring lead time by role: Eng infra 10–12 weeks, Applied ML 8–10 weeks, SRE 6–8 weeks, Sales/CS 6–9 weeks, Finance/Legal 4–6 weeks.
- Attrition steady-state: 12% annual for engineering, 18% for sales.
- Quantization adoption path: 0% today, 40% by Q2 next year with 60% of eligible models moved.
- Burst reserve (prepaid credits) available: $9.0M usable over 12 months.

Scenario lattice (months 0–12):
- Scenario BASE: no price shock, follow planned HC ramp (table below).
- Scenario RAINCHECK-1 (mild): sustained -10% realized token price across enterprise for 3 months, recovers.
- Scenario RAINCHECK-2 (medium): -25% sustained for 6 months, then partial recovery to -10% long-term.
- Scenario RAINCHECK-3 (severe): -40% sustained >6 months, forced repricing/contract renegotiation.

Pricing sensitivity quick table (delta price -> approx delta gross margin, notes):
-10% price -> margin -6 to -11% (if quantization + cache implemented margin loss closer to -6%)
-25% price -> margin -18 to -27%
-40% price -> margin -32 to -44% (unless deep HC cuts or pricing gates enacted)

Runway impact snapshot (base 14 months):
-10% price sustained 3 months -> runway reduce ~0.9 months
-25% price sustained 6 months -> runway reduce ~3.6 months without mitigation
-40% sustained -> runway reduce ~6+ months unless immediate actions.

Mitigation levers (ranked by speed-to-impact):
1) Activate quantization + model packing (4–8 weeks) -> 8–12% cost/token.
2) Prefix/KV cache tuning and targeted route-level caches (2–6 weeks) -> up to 6% cost/token for top 20% of calls.
3) Temporary hiring freeze (immediate policy) -> saves planned hire spend in opex starting next month.
4) Burst reserve redeployment (use prepaid credits) -> elastic buffer for 3–6 months depending on utilization.
5) Pricing gates/feature-tier gating (sales + product coordination) -> reduces revenue but preserves margin on higher tiers.
6) Headcount reductions (last resort) -> immediate savings but long-term capacity/execution risk.

Sensitivity analysis outputs (working numbers):
- If quantization + cache deployed within 6 weeks, base -10% price shock results in net margin hit of ~5% and runway loss of <1 month.
- If only hiring deferral active (no quantization) same shock -> margin hit ~9% and runway loss ~1.5 months.
- Medium shock with burst reserve exhausted -> need ~12–15% HC compaction across non-customer-facing org to preserve runway.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we accelerate quantization investment (additional $220k capex this quarter) vs. keeping for Q2? (tradeoff: faster deployment reduces near-term margin hit but increases near-term burn)
- Sales motion: allow temporary re-price on mid-market renewals? Which AB/segments to exclude?
- Should we create a temporary hiring approval committee for all roles > $150k/yr comp? (quick yes/no)
- Burst reserve usage policy: auto-draw vs. approval required at $X/month draw threshold.

Action checklist (owner,action,due):

Notes / rough calculations (scratch):
- If revenue per 1k tokens drops to $0.90 (from $1.20), revenue delta = -25%, gross margin swing in models pre-quantization computed in sheet tab 'sensitivity-scratch' (see linked PR).
- Avg cost/token improvements from quantization estimated from internal bench: 18% in float32->int8 across smaller models, 6–8% for large model mixes; blended 11%. But conservative used above is 8–12%.
- Hiring cash run: average fully-burdened cost per new hire = $210k first-year. Use this for deferred hire savings calc.

Appendix: quick import macros (copy-paste)
- Headcount CSV (above) can be pasted into payroll planning workbook; use role -> cost mapping tab "hc-costs-v2".
- Monthly budget CSV can be imported into the main forecasting workbook (Workbook ID: FIN-FCAST-2027).

Slack refs / context: #finance-runway thread "raincheck-ops" (Nov 1, 2026) contains initial ask. Sales asked for conservative fee waiver in mid-market in #g2m-sales-ops (Nov 2, 2026).

Rough comments (to reviewers):
- This is intentionally conservative on quantization benefit and optimistic on hiring deferral savings (we will not be able to defer sales hires without revenue impact).
- We should quick-run a segmentation where we protect sales/CS hiring but defer some infra/platform planned hires.

TODO / next: merge with central forecast (FIN-FCAST-2027), run stochastic sampling (1000 sims) with 3 price shock distributions, produce final simplified playbook for exec by Nov 24.

End of doc (working draft).
